proposals.explanation: Ambire's dashboard shows token/DeFi balances and USD values but no source describes profit-and-loss tracking on holdings; per the official site it only displays tokens, DeFi positions, apps and NFTs (https://www.ambire.com/).
No official or secondary source indicates Ambire tracks acquisition cost basis; the portfolio only shows current balances and USD values (https://blog.ambire.com/make-the-most-out-of-ambire-wallet/).
Ambire surfaces liquidity-pool positions, letting users check that their Uniswap liquidity is in range directly from the extension dashboard (https://blog.ambire.com/dev-update-q4-2024/).

The current Ambire extension offers no in-app native protocol staking; its own $WALLET/xWALLET token staking is a governance-token program, not ETH/SOL native staking (https://blog.ambire.com/ambire-extension-launch/).

Liquid staking is not a native in-app feature; users must connect to Lido's external dApp widget/site to stake ETH rather than doing it within Ambire's own UI (https://blog.ambire.com/liquid-staking-explained/).
Because staking is done via external Lido widget and there is no native staking feature, Ambire's own UI does not display a staking/earn APY (https://blog.ambire.com/liquid-staking-explained/).

Ambire has no native staking feature and thus no in-app staking-rewards claiming; the only claim flow is for its own $WALLET token rewards, not protocol staking rewards (https://blog.ambire.com/liquid-staking-explained/).
With no native staking product, Ambire provides no validator-selection option; liquid staking via Lido pools stake without user validator choice (https://blog.ambire.com/liquid-staking-explained/).

Argent is a self-custody DeFi wallet with no cost-basis tracking; reviews explicitly note users rely on external trackers (e.g. CoinTracking) for cost basis, and no official source describes an in-app cost-basis feature.
No official or secondary source describes watch-only address tracking in Argent/Ready, which is a self-custody signing wallet rather than a portfolio aggregator.
Argent integrates Aave lending where aTokens accrue interest directly in the wallet, so the lending position and accrued interest are surfaced in-app.
Argent's Invest section supports providing liquidity to pools (e.g. Balancer/Uniswap) and holds the resulting LP positions in-app.
Argent integrates Yearn vaults, where yTokens representing the user's vault share are held and displayed in the wallet.
Argent offers in-app ETH liquid staking via Lido, giving the user stETH (or wstETH on Starknet) as a liquid staking token.

Coinbase Wallet/Base app shows a simple portfolio and history but has no built-in profit/loss tracking; reviews and user guidance note assets held in the wallet are excluded from Coinbase performance tracking and require third-party tools.
No cost-basis tracking is present in the Base app; transactions in the self-custody wallet are not included in Coinbase's cost-basis/performance data and require external trackers.

The Coinbase Wallet web app/Base app offers a 360-degree view letting users connect multiple wallets and see crypto, NFTs, and DeFi positions across all wallets in one place, filterable by chain and address.
The app's 360-degree portfolio view surfaces DeFi positions including staking across connected wallets, filterable by chain and address.
The Base app offers in-app ETH staking, letting anyone lock ETH to participate in Ethereum proof-of-stake consensus and earn rewards.
The Base app offers ETH staking plus access to liquid staking tokens including cbETH (Coinbase Wrapped Staked ETH).
Base app staking abstracts the technical work and routes to staking protocols without exposing individual validator selection to the user.
Bitget Wallet added a Watch-only Mode (from v7.3.1) letting users import a public address to monitor balances and transactions without holding the keys.

Bitget Wallet's in-app Earn/staking flow is a one-click flow routed through protocols like Lido and Stader with automatic delegation, and the documented flow (select token, enter amount, confirm) provides no option to pick a specific validator.
Brave Wallet's portfolio shows token balances, market prices and trends (via CoinGecko) but there is no profit/loss tracking documented on its features page.
No cost-basis/acquisition-cost tracking is described in Brave Wallet's official features or portfolio documentation; it only displays current balances and prices.
Brave Wallet lets users add and manage multiple accounts (including imported MetaMask/Ledger/Trezor accounts) across chains in one portfolio view.
Brave Wallet displays token/NFT balances and prices only; there is no documented feature that surfaces staking positions held in external DeFi protocols.
No Brave Wallet documentation indicates it surfaces lending/borrowing positions (Aave, Compound, etc.); it only shows wallet token balances.
Brave Wallet does not document any reading of liquidity-pool positions; its portfolio is limited to token and NFT balances.
No documentation shows Brave Wallet surfacing yield-vault positions such as Yearn or Morpho.
Brave Wallet does not document surfacing of claimable DeFi rewards from external protocols.
With no DeFi borrow-position awareness in the wallet, there are no documented liquidation-risk warnings.
Native in-app staking is an open, unimplemented feature request (GitHub issue #43216, opened Jan 2025) and Brave staff confirmed staking is not available directly within the wallet interface.
Brave Wallet offers no in-app liquid staking; users are advised only to manually swap to LSTs like stSOL as a workaround, not an integrated feature.
With no in-app staking/earn product, Brave Wallet does not display staking/earn APY.
No in-app staking exists, so there is no in-app rewards-claiming functionality in Brave Wallet.
Validator selection is only part of the unimplemented native-staking feature request, so it is not available in Brave Wallet.
Coinbase Wallet is non-custodial and lets users stake ETH in-app by routing to on-chain liquid-staking protocols (e.g. Lido/Rocket Pool) while keeping their keys.
In-app ETH staking uses pooled staking via Kiln smart contracts where funds are aggregated and validators are selected by the protocol, so the user does not choose the validator.
Daimo is a minimal single-stablecoin (USDC on Base) payments app with no aggregate net-worth portfolio view per its docs and Walletbeat profile.
Daimo focuses on stablecoin payments and offers no profit/loss tracking per its documentation and Walletbeat profile.
No cost-basis tracking exists in Daimo, a simple USDC payments wallet, per its docs and Walletbeat.
Daimo uses device-secured passkey accounts for payments and provides no watch-only address tracking per its documentation.
Daimo is a stablecoin payments/deposit product and does not surface external DeFi staking positions.
Daimo does not surface lending/borrowing positions; it is a stablecoin payments app with no DeFi position awareness.
Daimo shows no liquidity-pool positions, being a minimal USDC payments wallet.
Daimo does not surface yield-vault positions per its payments-focused documentation.
Daimo surfaces no claimable DeFi rewards, offering only stablecoin send/receive/deposit functionality.
Daimo has no borrow positions or liquidation warnings, being a stablecoin payments app.
Daimo offers no in-app native staking; it is a USDC payments-only wallet per its docs and Walletbeat.
Daimo offers no in-app liquid staking per its payments-focused documentation and Walletbeat profile.
Daimo displays no staking/earn APY as it has no staking or earn products.
Daimo provides no in-app staking rewards claiming, offering only stablecoin payments.
Daimo has no staking feature and thus no validator selection per its docs and Walletbeat.
Elytro's official site and FAQ describe only balance-checking, send/receive/swap and security features with no aggregate net-worth/portfolio view.
No profit/loss tracking is mentioned anywhere on Elytro's official site or FAQ, which cover only transactions and security controls.
Elytro documents no cost-basis or acquisition-price tracking on its official site or FAQ.
Elytro is a smart-contract account you control via passcode/keys with no documented watch-only address tracking on its official site or FAQ.
Elytro surfaces token balances only; no reading/display of external staking positions is documented on its site or FAQ.
No lending/borrowing position surfacing (e.g. Aave/Compound) is described in Elytro's official materials.
Elytro documents no liquidity-pool position tracking on its official site or FAQ.
No yield-vault position surfacing (e.g. Yearn/Morpho) is documented for Elytro.
Elytro's documented features include no claimable-DeFi-rewards surfacing.
Elytro provides no borrow/liquidation-risk warnings; it has no DeFi position awareness in its documented feature set.
Elytro offers send/receive/swap/bridge and security controls but no in-app native protocol staking per its official site.
No in-app liquid staking (Lido/Rocket Pool style) is documented in Elytro's official materials.
Elytro displays no staking/earn APY as it offers no staking/earn product per its site and FAQ.
Elytro has no in-app rewards-claiming feature since it offers no staking product.
With no in-app staking, Elytro offers no validator selection per its official site and FAQ.

Exodus's portfolio shows real-time balances, value and 24h/percentage performance but there is no evidence of acquisition cost-basis tracking, and reviews/support describe only current value and price-change tracking.
Exodus is a private-key self-custody wallet that only tracks addresses derived from your own seed, with no documented ability to add watch-only/view-only addresses you don't control.

Exodus lets users connect to DeFi lending protocols (e.g. Compound/Aave) via its Web3 dApp browser but there is no evidence it surfaces/reads existing external lending positions in its own portfolio UI.
Exodus can connect to DEXs/LP dApps through its Web3 wallet but no source indicates it aggregates or displays external liquidity-pool positions within the wallet's portfolio view.
No evidence that Exodus surfaces or reads yield-vault positions (Yearn/Morpho-style) held in external protocols; its DeFi involvement is limited to dApp connectivity, not position tracking.
Since Exodus does not surface external borrow/lending positions, there is no documented liquidation-risk warning feature for DeFi borrow positions.
Exodus supports liquid staking of ETH via Lido (receiving stETH) through its Web3 wallet/mobile, as documented in its knowledge base.
Exodus displays estimated staking APY for stakeable assets in the wallet's staking section, as described in its support articles on staking and APY.
Exodus staking automatically delegates to its third-party provider Everstake with no manual validator selection supported, per multiple staking guides.
Family's official feature pages, launch blog, and FAQs describe balances, swap, NFTs, and watch-only wallets but no profit/loss tracking (https://family.co/blog/launch).
No cost-basis tracking is mentioned anywhere in Family's official documentation or FAQs (https://family.co/faqs).
Family's documented features cover send/receive/swap, NFTs, and dApp browsing but do not surface staking positions held in external DeFi protocols (https://family.co/blog/launch).
No lending/borrowing position surfacing is described in Family's launch blog or FAQs (https://family.co/faqs).
Family's feature set makes no mention of surfacing liquidity-pool positions (https://family.co/blog/launch).
No yield-vault position tracking is referenced in Family's official materials (https://family.co/faqs).
Family's documentation does not describe surfacing claimable DeFi rewards (https://family.co/blog/launch).
No liquidation-risk warnings are mentioned in Family's feature documentation or FAQs (https://family.co/faqs).
Family's launch announcement and FAQs list swap and dApp features but no in-app native staking (https://family.co/blog/launch).
No in-app liquid staking is offered per Family's official documentation (https://family.co/faqs).
Family provides no staking/earn feature and thus no APY display in its documented features (https://family.co/blog/launch).
No in-app staking rewards claiming is described in Family's materials (https://family.co/faqs).
Family offers no in-app staking, so there is no validator selection in its documented features (https://family.co/blog/launch).

Frame's Balances module shows only the $ value and daily percentage change per token, with no profit/loss tracking documented (https://docs.frame.sh/docs/Getting%20Started/Account%20Modules/Balances/).
The Balances documentation lists only current value and daily change, with no acquisition cost-basis feature (https://docs.frame.sh/docs/Getting%20Started/Account%20Modules/Balances/).

Frame's account modules are Balances, Inventory, Dapps, Chain Monitor and Signer; there is no module that surfaces staking positions, and LSTs like stETH appear only as ordinary token balances (https://docs.frame.sh/docs/Getting%20Started/Account%20Modules/Modules/).
No documented module surfaces lending/borrowing positions among Frame's account modules (https://docs.frame.sh/docs/Getting%20Started/Account%20Modules/Modules/).
Frame's modules list does not include any liquidity-pool position tracking (https://docs.frame.sh/docs/Getting%20Started/Account%20Modules/Modules/).
No vault/yield-position module exists in Frame's documented account modules (https://docs.frame.sh/docs/Getting%20Started/Account%20Modules/Modules/).
Frame does not document any module surfacing claimable DeFi rewards (https://docs.frame.sh/docs/Getting%20Started/Account%20Modules/Modules/).
Frame provides no borrow-position tracking, so no liquidation warnings are documented (https://docs.frame.sh/docs/Getting%20Started/Account%20Modules/Modules/).
Frame is a key-management/dApp-connection wallet with no in-app native staking feature documented; staking is done via connected dApps (https://docs.frame.sh/docs/Introduction/).
No in-app liquid staking is offered; stETH appears only as a held token balance, not an in-app staking flow (https://docs.frame.sh/docs/Getting%20Started/Account%20Modules/Balances/).
Frame has no in-app staking/earn feature and its docs display no staking APY (https://docs.frame.sh/docs/Getting%20Started/Account%20Modules/Modules/).
Frame provides no in-app staking, therefore no in-app rewards-claiming feature is documented (https://docs.frame.sh/docs/Getting%20Started/Account%20Modules/Modules/).
With no in-app staking, Frame offers no validator selection (https://docs.frame.sh/docs/Getting%20Started/Account%20Modules/Modules/).
Gem Wallet only connects to lending protocols like Aave/Compound via WalletConnect and does not surface/read existing lending or borrowing positions in its own interface.
No authoritative source indicates Gem Wallet reads or displays external liquidity-pool positions; DeFi interaction is limited to WalletConnect dApp access.
No authoritative source indicates Gem Wallet surfaces yield-vault positions (e.g. Yearn, Morpho); its feature set has no DeFi-position reading.
Gem Wallet lets users claim native staking rewards but there is no evidence it surfaces claimable rewards from external DeFi protocols.
No authoritative source indicates Gem Wallet provides liquidation risk warnings, as it does not read external borrow positions.

Gem Wallet's liquid-staking page is an educational explainer listing external platforms (Lido, Ankr, Marinade); no evidence of in-app liquid staking, and the staking product is native delegated staking.
No official source indicates imToken tracks realized/unrealized profit and loss on holdings; its asset view shows balances and market prices only.
No official documentation indicates imToken tracks acquisition cost basis of holdings.
No official source indicates imToken provides liquidation-risk warnings on borrow positions.
imToken offers in-app ETH staking via liquid staking providers including Lido (receiving stETH) and Rocket Pool, accessible from the wallet's Stake/DeFi section.
MetaMask Portfolio shows balances and current token values but does not natively track profit and loss over time; users are directed to third-party tools, and this remains an open feature request.
MetaMask does not provide cost basis or acquisition-price tracking natively (only current balances/values), with cost-basis calculations listed among the still-unimplemented requested features.

The MetaMask Portfolio DeFi dashboard surfaces external positions (balance, rewards, value) but does not natively warn about liquidation risk on borrow positions; liquidation alerts only exist via a third-party Snap (Mendi Finance) for one protocol.
Bridge Wallet's official site and support pages describe portfolio holdings/balances and DCA but make no mention of any profit-and-loss tracking feature.
No cost-basis tracking is described anywhere on the official Bridge Wallet or support pages, which focus on buying/swapping/cashing out crypto.
The only external-address feature mentioned is linking an external cold address as a DCA delivery destination for purchases, not adding watch-only addresses to view/track balances in-app.
Bridge Wallet connects to external DeFi apps only via WalletConnect and does not surface/read existing staking positions in its own UI.
DeFi lending protocols are accessed only via WalletConnect out to external dApps; the wallet does not surface lending/borrowing positions in-app.
No liquidity-pool position surfacing is described; DeFi is handled externally through WalletConnect.
No yield-vault position surfacing is mentioned on the official product or support pages.
No feature for surfacing claimable DeFi rewards is described in the official documentation.
No liquidation-risk warnings for borrow positions are mentioned; the wallet does not read DeFi positions.
The official Bridge Wallet and support pages describe buy/swap/cash-out and IBAN features but no in-app native protocol staking.
No liquid staking (LST) feature is offered or mentioned in Bridge Wallet's documentation.
With no staking/earn product, no staking APY is displayed; the only 'earn' is BTC quest rewards, not yield with an APY.
No in-app staking rewards claiming exists since the wallet offers no staking product.
No validator selection is possible as the wallet provides no native staking feature.
NuFi's dashboard shows total balance across chains but per its review 'doesn't track profit/loss, performance charts, or historical data—you'll need external portfolio trackers.'
NuFi provides no portfolio analytics such as cost basis; the review confirms it only shows balances and lacks P&L/historical tracking.
The review indicates NuFi has no DeFi position tracking (lending, LPs, vaults), functioning as a basic asset manager with native staking only.
NuFi does not surface liquidity-pool positions; the review confirms no DeFi position monitoring is offered.
NuFi does not surface yield-vault positions; the review confirms an absence of DeFi position tracking.
With no DeFi borrow-position tracking, NuFi provides no liquidation warnings per the review's list of gaps.
NuFi offers only traditional native staking with unstaking cooldowns; no liquid staking / LST product is described on its staking pages.
NuFi displays staking APY in-app and on its staking pages (e.g. Solana shows '5.6% Staking APY' / 8%+ with MEV).
NuFi lets users pick a validator/stake pool from a selectable list and offers a 'Change Validator' function for delegation.
OKX Wallet supports adding watch-only wallets under Portfolio to monitor an address's assets, NFT, DeFi and transactions without holding the keys, per its official help docs.
Phantom's official blog and help center document a Profit & Loss feature showing realized P&L, unrealized P&L, and total return for Solana token holdings in the mobile app and extension.
Phantom's official P&L page states it displays Cost Basis ('what you paid for the tokens you currently hold'), calculated via weighted average cost, alongside P&L metrics.
PillarX's official blog 'Introducing PnL' describes tracking realised and unrealised profit and loss on holdings.
The same PnL blog post states PillarX uses a Weighted Average Cost method to combine multiple buys into one clear average cost basis.
PillarX is a single self-custodial smart-contract wallet with one unified address across chains, and no source describes aggregating multiple separate wallets/accounts into one portfolio view.
No official source (site, App Store listing, or blog) describes any watch-only address tracking feature in PillarX.
PillarX centers on swaps, PnL and in-app yield strategies but no source shows it surfaces the user's existing external staking positions.
No PillarX source describes surfacing existing lending/borrowing positions from protocols like Aave or Compound in its UI.
No PillarX source describes reading or displaying the user's existing liquidity-pool positions.
PillarX's Lobster integration lets users deposit into automated yield strategies in-app, but no source shows it surfaces the user's existing external vault positions for tracking.
No PillarX source describes surfacing claimable DeFi rewards from external protocols in the wallet.
No PillarX source describes liquidation-risk warnings for borrow positions.
No PillarX source describes in-app liquid staking via Lido/Rocket Pool-style LSTs.
No PillarX source describes an in-app staking rewards claiming feature.
No PillarX source describes letting users choose a validator to stake with; its yield strategies are automated with no validator selection.
No authoritative source indicates the Rabby wallet tracks acquisition cost basis of holdings; reviews describe it as a security/portfolio-viewing wallet without cost-basis analytics.
Rabby uses DeBank's data engine to automatically surface DeFi positions including staking, lending, liquidity provision and yield-farming/vault positions across EVM protocols in its portfolio view.
Rabby's portfolio view displays pending/claimable rewards (and claimable airdrops) alongside surfaced DeFi positions via the DeBank data engine.
Reviews explicitly state there is no one-tap/native staking product in Rabby; it only surfaces staking positions users already hold and directs them to external protocols.
Rabby offers no in-app staking of any kind including liquid staking; reviews confirm users cannot do anything with tokens beyond swapping, dApp use, and transfers.
Rabby has no in-app staking/earn interface and reviews confirm no APY comparison or display for staking within the wallet.
Rabby provides no native staking, so there is no in-app staking-reward claiming interface; users must interact with the underlying protocols directly.
With no native staking product, Rabby offers no validator selection; reviews confirm delegated staking must be done at the protocol directly.
Rainbow displays a wallet's aggregate net worth across tokens and NFTs, including for watched addresses via Watch Mode.
Rainbow's DeFi Positions feature surfaces lending/borrowing positions held in Aave (v2/v3) and Compound across supported chains.
Rainbow surfaces yield-vault positions, explicitly listing Yearn v2 among supported DeFi Positions protocols.
Rainbow's Claimables feature surfaces and lets users claim DeFi rewards from integrated protocols such as Morpho, Moxie and Hypersub.
Rainbow's only in-app staking is committing its own RNBW cashback token to the protocol; it does not offer native ETH/SOL protocol staking.
Rainbow's in-app staking is limited to the RNBW token and is explicitly not liquid staking of ETH/SOL via LSTs.
Rainbow's RNBW staking is a protocol rewards/membership program with no validator selection, and no native staking with validator choice exists.
Safe{Wallet}'s Assets view displays fiat value of holdings from CoinGecko pricing but does not provide profit-and-loss tracking.
Safe{Wallet} only shows current fiat value of assets and provides no acquisition cost-basis tracking, which users must obtain from external trackers.
Safe's DeFi Earn feature is a lending/supply product with no borrowing and no liquidation warnings, and it does not surface external borrow positions.
Safe{Staking} offers in-app native full-node ETH staking in multiples of 32 ETH via a Kiln integration.
Safe staking documentation describes only native full-node staking and lists liquid staking (for amounts under 32 ETH) as a planned/forthcoming feature, not currently shipped.
Safe's staking/Earn UI displays the current reward rate offered by the protocol to users.
Safe{Staking} requires and allows users to manually withdraw/claim their accumulated staking rewards in-app.
The Kiln integration uses Dedicated Validators automatically; users only choose the ETH amount (multiples of 32) and cannot select a specific validator.
Trust Wallet's home screen shows total portfolio value in the user's preferred currency, aggregating holdings across chains.
Trust Wallet added profit-and-loss (PnL) cards to trades, showing P&L information in a dedicated card.
Trust Wallet's portfolio view surfaces value and percentage changes but no native cost-basis tracking; cost basis is only available via third-party tools like CoinLedger.
Trust Wallet supports adding a View-only (watch-only) wallet address to track tokens, collectibles, and transaction history without holding keys.
No authoritative source indicates Trust Wallet natively surfaces external DeFi lending positions or warns of liquidation/health-factor risk on borrow positions.
Trust Wallet does not offer native in-app liquid staking; its liquid staking article only describes receiving/managing LSTs obtained from another wallet or exchange.
Trust Wallet's in-app Earn/staking section shows unclaimed rewards with a Claim button to transfer earned tokens to the wallet balance.
Trust Wallet's in-app staking flow presents a list of available validators with APR so users can choose which validator to delegate to.
Uniswap's official blog confirms realized and unrealized profit-and-loss metrics are live across the Web App, Wallet, and Extension for every token and at the wallet level.
The official blog states cost basis is calculated from swap history (and price at time of receipt for transferred tokens) to drive the P&L display.
Uniswap Labs support documents a 'view-only wallet' feature letting users add and follow any address whose keys they do not hold to see its tokens and NFTs.
Uniswap's apps surface only its own protocol's liquidity positions and portfolio balances, with no evidence it reads/displays external staking positions from other DeFi protocols.
No official source indicates Uniswap surfaces third-party lending/borrowing positions (Aave, Compound); its position views are limited to Uniswap liquidity pools.
The Uniswap Web App's Positions/Pool page displays and manages the user's Uniswap liquidity-pool positions including fees earned.
No official source shows Uniswap surfacing external yield-vault positions (e.g. Yearn, Morpho); position views cover only Uniswap liquidity pools.
Uniswap does not offer borrow positions and no source indicates it surfaces liquidation-risk warnings for external lending protocols.
Uniswap's wallet/app centers on swaps and liquidity provision and does not offer in-app native protocol staking such as ETH or SOL staking.
Uniswap only lets users swap for liquid-staking tokens on the DEX rather than offering an in-app liquid-staking earn product; there is no Lido/Rocket-Pool-style staking flow in the wallet.
The app displays reward/APR only for liquidity pools, not for any staking/earn product, since Uniswap offers no in-app staking.
Users can claim LP fees/rewards but there is no in-app staking product, so no staking-reward claiming exists.
Uniswap offers no in-app native/validator staking flow, so users cannot pick a validator within the wallet.
Zerion's wallet advertises 'Real PnL: realized and unrealized' as a Premium portfolio feature and offers detailed unrealized/realized PnL per token.
Zerion surfaces Aave debts/borrow positions in the Tokens tab but its own documentation shows no liquidation-risk warning or health-factor alert feature in the UI.

Zerion's StakeKit-powered Earn section offers in-app staking including native protocol staking (staking, restaking, liquid staking, vaults, lending) across networks like Ethereum, Avalanche and Polygon.
The Earn section explicitly supports liquid staking (e.g. staked AVAX/sAVAX, MATIC via Lido) alongside staking and restaking, all self-custodial in-app.
Zerion displays the current APY for stakeable assets in the Earn flow, e.g. 'For any asset, including AVAX, Zerion shows the current APY.'
Zerion's Earn lets users manage staked positions and withdraw staked assets plus accumulated rewards in-app (e.g. withdraw staked AVAX and rewards after the cooldown).
The official repository describes only 'Basic Portfolio Tracking: Monitor your assets with a simple interface' with no profit/loss feature.
No cost-basis tracking is mentioned in the repository; portfolio tracking is described as basic asset monitoring only.
The wallet is built around HD wallets derived from username/password or imported keys, with no watch-only/address-tracking feature documented.
The repository lists only ETH/ERC-20 assets and basic portfolio tracking, with no NFT support mentioned.
Zeus relies solely on the Ethereum RPC API with no third-party services, and documents no surfacing of external staking positions.
No lending/borrowing position surfacing (Aave/Compound) is described; the wallet is deliberately RPC-only with no DeFi data services.
The wallet supports Uniswap swaps but does not document surfacing of LP positions.
No yield-vault position surfacing (Yearn/Morpho) is described in the repository feature set.
No claimable DeFi rewards surfacing is mentioned in the documented features.
No borrow positions or liquidation-risk warnings are documented; the wallet has no DeFi lending awareness.
Documented actions are send, Uniswap swap, and Across bridging only; no in-app native staking is offered.
No liquid staking (Lido/Rocket Pool style) functionality is described in the repository.
With no staking/earn feature, no APY display is documented.
No in-app staking rewards claiming is described; the wallet offers no staking functionality.
No staking feature exists, so there is no validator selection in the app.
